item.title: A Sadist Cap [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes?

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: My SCP is a dunce cap that can telepathically talk to their victims and tricks them that it's a higher being, and if they do what it demands, they'll be gifted eternal salvation. When the victim completes their task(s), the SCP disappears and leaves them, so they can suffer for what they have done. (So basically, it's a troll)

Central Narrative: In 1990, a man was found dead in his house from suicide. One of his friends went to check on him and saw that the door was unlocked. He decided to enter the house and noticed there were multiple drawings all over the walls and hand-made wooden objects related to the SCP scattered around the room. There was also a message on one of the walls that say this,

"I Don't Understand. I Did Everything It Wanted Me To Do, But I Don't Hear It Anymore. I Made It My God. I Pushed Everyone Away From My Life. I Killed My Own Two Kids For It, And Yet It's Abandons Me. I Guess My Fate Wasn't Good Enough…"

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The cap can somehow teleport to different places in the world, causing more harm to others. The cap does these things to people because it finds it entertaining. The SCP only goes after religious people.

Additional Notes: This might be a boring and cringy SCP idea, so go easy on me lol. (But seriously though, any critique is helpful.)

I don't think I represented my central narrative the right way, but the story is going to be around addendums, interviews, and incidents.

Should I change the object the SCP is? I don't think a dunce cap would fit too well. it seems silly IMO…

item.title: Fireproof Rescue Dog
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Containment Procedures, Description, Recovered Incident Reports, Email Transcript

Genre: Dramatic, with some lighthearted moments between the dog and it’s handler

Elevator Pitch:

+ Show Elevator Pitch
- Hide Elevator Pitch

This SCP is a former SAR (Search and Rescue) dog that is completely unaffected by fire and smoke. When irritated, the dog is also able to raise its internal body temperature to an unnaturally high level, allowing it to essentially burn those who come into contact with it and spit small sparks. Visually, the dog is a completely average looking dalmatian. Given that it was an SAR animal, the dog had a handler. However, the handler was entirely non-anomalous and ignorant of the animal's abilities. The dog and the handler were close with the local fire department and went on missions almost exclusively related to local fires and their aftermaths.

Central Narrative:

+ Show Central Narrative
- Hide Central Narrative

The central narrative of this SCP Article would be the history of the SCP’s life prior to containment. This would be told through the local fire department’s incident reports recovered by the Foundation, detailing calls the dog was used on and how the dog and it’s handler performed. The reports would be written by the dog’s handler and would detail their specific experiences working with the dog during the incident. The handler is entirely human and simply good at their job. The dog’s anomalous protection does not extend to them nor anything other than itself.

The dog is contained by the Foundation after it gives several children second and third degree burns. This happens because of an off-duty incident when the dog and it’s handler are approached by a mother and her three children while relaxing at a park. The handler is distracted talking with the mother, while the children entertain themselves with the dog. Eventually, the dog becomes irritated by the attention and attacks them, biting one child and barking at the rest. This would result in the bitten child having a severe third degree burn from the bite and the other two children having small second degree burns from the dog’s saliva, sprayed from its barking. This portion of the story would be told by a hospital’s incident report that is also recovered by the Foundation.

This incident is what alerts the Foundation to the dog’s existence. The dog is subsequently contained, with it’s handler and any witnesses to the incident are anesthetized.

The article would end several years after the dog is contained, with a researcher in charge of the animal noting its declining health and mental state. The researcher makes a request to their superiors to suggest the dog be used for SAR work once again, this time for the Foundation. This portion of the article is told through an email.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ Show Hook/Attention-Grabber
- Hide Hook/Attention-Grabber

I want the reader to feel bad for this SCP. It’s just an animal born with powers it can’t quite control. The dog only wants to help people and be with its handler, but that can’t be because of the dangers present with its abilities.

Additional Notes:

+ Show Additional Notes
- Hide Additional Notes

My plan is to make this article fairly straightforward and short given that this is my first. I’m not expecting it to be greenlit quite yet, but I would appreciate any continued criticism or suggestion. In particular, whether the concept seems viable or whether I should rewrite the concept entirely.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlights) scpwiki.com
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

Elevator Pitch: scpwiki.com is a website created by The Foundation where creative writers post articles and tales detailing a fictional universe populated by anomalous items, entities and groups of interest, with the SCP Foundation at the heart.

Central Narrative: The Foundation created the website after online discussions of the SCP Foundation emerged, with the aim of protecting the masquerade by decieving people into believing it was fictional. However, a shift from SCP-507 reveals it to be anomalous, and responsible for creating events and anomalies in an alternate universe and its own SCP Foundation, leaving The Foundation to ponder if they are any different.

Hook/ Attention-Grabber: I want to ask a question that (please correct me if I'm wrong!) I haven't yet seen on the site; what if the Foundation exists in our world, and the site is merely for readers to be decieved into believing it does not exist? It fundamentally links our world and the fictional world in a very literal way.

Additional Notes: Again, I cannot say I am hugely well-read on the site, and so it is possible an article similar to this exists, for which I apologise- it is a coincidence. But I do believe that it has potential (and even considered storing it for when I had more experience writing and proposing it for 001, but I don't think it would stand its ground, and I'm impatient!).

item.title: Re: Damian Thorne's Needlessly [REDACTED] Intro
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Damian Thorne! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

Well, keep your secrets to yourself then - regardless though, welcome to the site. I'd really want to say something more, but without your input, I can't really do much here. I'll say this much - I very much hope you enjoy your time here on-site and achieve all of the goals you're aiming for.

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action.

Page Layout (Optional): I plan on using Audio and journal entries made by a person who can't stop "Switching Channels"

Elevator Pitch: The core idea is, got a remote off an elecric devices shop. he uses the remote he got and teleports into random universes since the teleportation remote is broken. And he is trying to get home fast.

Central Narrative: A normal guy bought a new TV remote. When he came home he saw some strange letters on the buttons, although the TV remote looked normal he soon finds out that it is not normal. Some letters were scratched off he thought it was probably because of shipping or any other reason. untill he used it. He saw a flashing light and then he is back in his apartment. Well "His" is not the right answer. He turned on the TV and found that he is not in "His" home. The tv message said that the sun is corrupted and it turns all biological life-forms into a pile of flesh that tries to get people corrupted. He did not know how to react he grabbed "His" backpack and journal. When he was about to leave he looked at his Very normal remote. He pressed it to turn off the TV since the other remote was too far. A flash, and he is not in that nightmerish world… this time it might be worse.

+ Show more
- Show less

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The attention grabber here is obviously the remote he got. and it's ability to let him teleport to random universes. I seen people and objects going into other dimensions. But never objects or people going into diffrent universes.

Additional Notes: None

item.title: Good idea, but...
item.content:encoded:
You will need to work on your writing style a bit.

+ writing style
- writing style

You do not have a big problem with scientific language, but there are some big scratches to polish out of existence.

Sometimes you use very good sounding words like "homicide" but in the very same sentence you say kids instead of children. Such minor informalities spoil the experience a bit. But there are some bigger concerns too.

Especially the lower part of the description sounds like a videogame.
For example:
"a larger than normal strength level"
or
"It needs three medium- sized bullets to the head to be penetrated"

As a self proclaimed weapons expert the second sentence gives me a headache. What are medium sized bullets? 7,62mm? 12,7mm? How thick has a skull made of bones to be for being impenetrable by one 12,7mm bullet? Where did the test shots hit? Front, Side, Back? You get the point. And what is a normal strength level? Why do these SCP-5580-2 have to be exactly 2 meters tall? Nature doesn't draw straight lines.

Don't get me wrong, its an fabulous story to tell at the ceasefire, but for the SCP-Universe it is just not scientific enough. Implant some figures (like the ones above), do some research on what you are scribing about. And if there are no exact figures, scribe: SCP-5580-2 are "approximately" 2 meters tall.

Furthermore try to ban the word "and" a bit. Proofreading, you will stumble upon sections, in which you have aight sentences in a row, connected with "and" to four sentences. This looks a bit unprofessional.

Finally I want to talk about what this SCP really has a problem with: It has no special context whatsoever. What many people need to learn is, that we are not reading these SCP-articles to experience thrilling brutality, or look at cool monsters. There are countless horror films that do a better job with that. We, the people reading about SCPs want a story. Imagine a horror film without a story. There are such films out there, that give you two hours of scary dullness. You don't want that.

Here is an idea how you can make your SCPs story more unique, because I am pretty sure that someone already came up with something similar. There are over 5000 SCPs out there.

The story of discovery has some thrilling degree in it. Use the fact, that children often say exactly what they think. Make some interviews with them. Give them a major role in the story. Way more interesting than just a random dude. Or ad a researcher who started friendship-relations with the children and recovered them from the evil (or perhaps failed). Add some feeling, some character-development, some story.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: My first SCP

I agree that this does have some promise, but doesn't quite manage to deliver. Keep working on that potential.

item.title: Re: Possible Keter Class article Hurricane Omega
item.content:encoded:
I think my primary issue here is honestly that your triggering scenario isn't unlikely enough, because global warming is really, really bad.

This past season, which I'm assuming was part of the inspiration, we reached 30 named storms. That's an outlier even by today's standards, but the thing is, typical Atlantic Tropical Storm Seasons in the past few decades have been comparable to some of the worst hurricane seasons in the late 1800's/early 1900's, even accounting for the spottier record keeping in ye olden days. There's an upward trend, and it's accelerating.

It's not a matter of if we'll hit a season with hurricane omega, it's whether it happens by 2040 or not.

There still might be a solid idea here, but I'd suggest looking at a more abstract trigger than just reaching the end of the name list- Say, the Foundation has identified some unlikely pattern of storm paths that would summon the storm equivalent of Cthulhu (so more storms means more chances that it could happen).

item.title: (Seeking Greenlights) Decieve Me Not
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

+ Elevator Pitch
- Elevator Pitch

Decieve Me Not is a sapient humanoid entity that is believed to be a unique and poorly understood type of reality bender. It appears to be wearing a crimson robe and a white, porcelain Greek comedy mask. It has near-perfect control over its abilities, but these abilities appear to be limited to a specific few. It can teleport, which is countered by SRAs. Its main anomalous trait, however, is its ability to control and affect minds, which cannot be countered with SRAs. During conversation with the entity, an individual is compelled to tell the truth to any question the entity may ask. The other ability is long term- after viewing or hearing it at a present state (i.e., not through recording or photograph), an individual will undergo anomalous mental changes over three weeks. They will begin to lie intermittently, before eventually losing the ability to tell the truth. They will then seek out conversation with the entity, leading to them lying to it, resulting in [DATA EXPUNGED].

+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

The narrative largely revolves around unraveling the nature of the entity, with a short side note of an unfortunate doctor whose life was effectively ruined by its anomalous effects. It strangely appeared in a Foundation site, seemingly willing to be contained and thus interrogated. It takes a number of individuals to be affected until the Foundation can effectively contain it, however, at which point they attempt to unravel its goals and nature, with a certain Foundation doctor being brought in for his ability to combat its anomalous effects and research it. Hints are gradually made throughout the article that it is in fact at the whim of an unidentified, much more powerful reality bender, and that the entity itself aims to make itself more powerful so that he may usurp the more powerful one. Furthermore, more hints (especially the entity's appearance and an O5 classified interview at the end) imply that the entity is linked to The Hanged King, and specifically one of his three lords.

+ Hook/ Attention-Grabber
- Hook/ Attention-Grabber

The article aims to explore the theme of truth and lies, both showing how that may affect normal individuals on a more mundane basis, and how they may be percieved by entities of a higher existence. Furthermore, I hope to hook readers with a gradually unravelling plot of deception, which, even by the end, is not fully explained, leaving readers to their own imagination.

+ Additional Notes
- Additional Notes

The article may seem fairly ambitious for a first time writer, which I understand. I have a few other ideas for SCPs which I will pursue while I await greenlights, and if you believe that the idea is good but do not have faith in a first time writer to properly execute it, I would appreciate that feedback, though I would love the opportunity to put forward a draft.

Conceptually speaking, this article doesn't really make itself unique. The anomaly just seems to be a bigger, sentient Earth that absorbs planets and materials in order to grow in mass. Theres no further explanation. Nothing for the reader to latch onto or really get involved with. The length doesn't really do it justice in this regard.

Logically, I'm unsure of how researchers would be able to identify that this planet has sentience. Did they go to it and interview it? How do they know that its absorbing mass? There are just a lot of open-ended statements with no real investigation or investment logically to back them up. The suspension of disbelief ultimately broke for me as I read it.

If you decide to rewrite this, I would heavily advocate for expansion. Remove the redactions and the expungments, give us a story, or something more than an empty conceptual trope. Anomalys like this need something to back them up, especially if you're intending to make it short-form. An emotional impact, a conceptually unique or wacky punchline, just anything more than "whoa, neat."

EDIT: Should further mention that including the "O5" in the Containment Procedures just seems like a poor attempt at escalating the "threat" of your anomaly. Theres really no reason behind it, as far as I can tell. Honestly, nothing about the Conprocs actually describe how to contain it at all. Which, is a little weird for me. TL;DR this is just a conceptually boring trope with no story or investment besides it being "cool." You should really try to put a spin on this and include something to attach the readers with, or try a new anomaly (or even expand your wordcount to include addenda and exploration).

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Uncontainable Man
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify)

Page Layout: Alternating between versions of the Uncontainable Man's SCP file and prose sections detailing the Foundation's encounters with him.

Elevator Pitch: A man who literally cannot be contained. If anyone tries to hold him against his will, something will always happen that lets him get out, no matter how many ridiculous coincidences have to happen together. This man is incredibly arrogant and attempts to use this power to toy with the Foundation to get what he wants – at least until he learns why the numebr-one rule of messing with the Foundation is, "Don't."

Central Narrative: The narrative starts with an MTF being dispatched to Somerandomtown County (working name) to investigate reports of a prisoner in the county jail who's anomalously good at escaping. They track down the prisoner, tell him who they are, handcuff him, and take him to Site-8 for containment. After a week, a containment breach occurs at Site-8, letting him out. The MTF recaptures him, and the cycle of containment, escape, and recapture repeats as the Foundation creates harsher and harsher conprocs, until they figure out what's going on and decide to put out a reward for whoever can devise conprocs for this man. Eventually, the captain of the MTF, who at this point is sick of chasing this guy, asks him what the Foundation has to do to contain him. At this point, the guy starts making ridiculous demands to the tune of "you have to contain me in a five-star hotel and give me anything I ask for, no matter how ridiculous-" and then the captain just shoots him. Finally, the article ends with the SCP's updated containment file, with the class as Neutralized and the Special Containment Procedures being, "If it doesn't comply, threaten lethal force."

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Explores what would actually happen if the Foundation encountered an anomaly whose property is that he cannot be contained, and also tries to derive humor from some old Gary Stu cliches ("my original chaructr is a humanid wat will DSTROIE EVERYSANG and BRETCH CONTEINMENT IF THE FONDANTION DOESNT GIV IT WHAT IT WANTS).

item.title: Re: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

Page 1

SCP-XXXX is the first spacecraft observed by the Foundation.

As in the first ever spacecraft they ever witnessed or just the first one they witnessed for this SCP? Confused by the wording here.

Considering this is a listpages SCP, I know there's more to come and the first page gives so little info, it serves as a good, 'wait, something isn't right…' page, if you know what I mean. Even without the knowledge of listpages, I think it's still just 'off' enough to give the reader the sense that something isn't right.

The clinical is a bit iffy, though. I apologise that I'm doing a more 'general thoughts' crit and not a true in-depth LBL.

Mainly the bits that bothered me were:

new telescope parts like refractors

I feel like 'such as' would be better than 'like'

SCP-XXXX has a frame in the form between a cylinder and an oblate spheroid.

'between a' is what sounds sub-clinical to me. I'm sure there's a better word to use there…sadly, I'm not that great at clinical tone either, so I kinda…can't think of a suitable replacement for that :U

On the bottom side is a small outer room

The adjective 'small' is what bothers me, as I've read somewhere that most adjectives aren't clinical.

Page 2

Immediately, I find myself significantly more intrigued by this page. I know you said you had problems with Page 2, but I really like it so far.

Upon arrival, SCP-XXXX-1 will make said star disappear by unknown means.

'make said star disappear' is vastly unclinical.

How does it make them disappear? By touch?

If so, 'Upon contact with SCP-XXXX-1, stars will immediately vanish. How this occurs is currently unknown.' would be better. But again, I'm no clinical tone pro.

Due to the lesser quality of amnestics at the time, Ferdinand von Zeppelin did not suffer from complete memory-loss and had a few fragments left of SCP-XXXX in his subconsciousness.

That…is such a fucking cool headcanon you thought of. I love this touch. A lot. Zeppelins are the vague hint towards this SCPs existence. I think that's brilliant.

Currently, the LZ 127 Zeppelin represents SCP-XXXX the most accurate.

'Currently, SCP-XXXX is most accurately represented by the LZ 127 Zeppelin.'

On 28 August 1903, several researchers educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX near the Orion Arm. Upon showing von Zeppelin their findings, it was confirmed that this was indeed the same object he saw 30 years ago. He was then administered amnestics again, this time resulting in the permanent loss of his memories of SCP-XXXX.

I would just remove this bit. No way the Foundation would show someone an anomaly only to re-amnesticize them again. I don't buy it. Also, we already know that SCP-XXXX is confirmed to be what he saw, so this is unnecessary and repeats info we already know.

Page 2 is pretty good so far. Definitely a good jump from Page 1. I'll go ahead and read Page 3 and I'll let you know how it stacks up.

Page 3

SCP-XXXX is a dark metallic spacecraft roaming through space with one passenger, designated as SCP-XXXX-1 on board

'SCP-XXXX is a dark metallic spacecraft roaming through space with one passenger on board, designated SCP-XXXX-1.'

Also, I really like this bit. This definitely wasn't something I saw coming.

ALSO, HAVE YOU THOUGH OF A NAME YET?

Thought*

YOU HAVE ALWAYS GIVEN ME THE SAME NAME.

- GLEN, SCP-XXXX-1, THE RESETTER OF THE UNIVERSE

That was a twist and a half and I fucking love it and it genuinely gives me motivation to continue my own ambitious as hell listpages SCP.

Thank you for sharing this draft with me.

As for the falling action with the O5 sending Glen the godspeed message…idk how to feel about that.

I really like the idea of an anomaly that can't be contained and is universally recognized as good, but at the same time, idk if this is the most realistic reaction the O5 would have.

Either way, the implications, Glen, and the twist at the end is all superb.

Even with the issues I stated above, that twist at the end would have easily earned my upvote.

I think it all works as a whole, just need polish in all the right areas and you're golden.

I didn't stay to deeply examine the dialogue further, but it's definitely improving significantly.

Either way, I hope I helped. Good luck with the rest of this skip, dude. You got this.

👍

item.title: (SEEKING GREENLIGHTS) Questionable Infohazard
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Typical SCP article including logs of every asked question, their host's reactions, and outcomes.

+Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention Grabber, and Notes
- why?

Elevator Pitch: The anomaly is an infohazard that induces a great sense of curiosity to individuals who have gained any information regarding it. Individuals with knowledge of the SCP initially ask themselves a certain question, regardless of which it is unknown to the individual or not, or classified or not. The subjects have no control over whatever question they ask. That is known as Stage 1 of the "infection". Stage 2 makes the individual have a great urge in research, usually that of the question they asked themselves. In certain individuals, Stage 3 may manifest. Stage 3 is death by insanity, believed to have been caused by the exponential growth of their will to find information or their "ultimate answer" to their questions. Stage 3 is only known to manifest if ever an individual asks themselves a certain impossibility, or possibly classified information. The infohazard is only lethal whenever an individual expires after 3 years of infection.

Central Narrative: The infohazard was detected after a lack of personnel morale. Plenty of personnel was observed asking "why" to themselves, with the situation growing large enough to be taken into consideration by the O5 council. Journals were distributed to affected personnel in an attempt to learn the nature of the phenomenon. The journals contain the questions, reactions, and outcomes of the personnel.

Examples:

Dr. █████

Q: Why did ███████ cheat on me?
R: Disappointed
O: Has found answer after interrogating Dr. ███████

Janitor ██████████

Q: How did O5-12 even get to █████████?
R: Confused
O: Janitor ██████████ was detained and taken into custody, interviewed. O5-12 then administered Class A amnestics

Dr. ███

Q: Why did Wondertainment make the █████████████ product line?
R: Extreme confusion
O: Subject was unable to recieve an answer, thus requesting amnestics.

Dr. ███████████

Q: How did SCP-█████ go to that other narrative?
R: Confused, striken with anxiety
O: Detained, interrogated by O5-██, was administered Class B amnestics. O5-██ claims it as a good way to determine possible future SCP's

Hook/Attention Grabber: A very dangerous or beneficial infohazard, causes great curiosity among the infected. Causes you to question anything, everything.

Additional notes: I'd prefer this article to be a great motivation when it comes to philosophical ideals, and the act of always questioning. But why?
